Composable calendar presentation and anchored ages

Source: R/dates.R
omop_date_spec.Rd

Date declarations execute privately on each server. Calendar periods are ordered factors by default; number supplies trend coordinates, and start/end supplies inclusive period bounds. Exact ages use completed anniversaries (February 29 uses March 1 in non-leap years). Missing partial dates give NA unless a policy is declared. All patient-linked results retain class 2. Variable fields override recipe fields, then design defaults.

Usage

omop_date_spec(
  precision = NULL,
  representation = NULL,
  numeric = NULL,
  origin = NULL,
  anchor = NULL,
  pattern = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  level_range = NULL,
  fiscal_start = NULL,
  week_start = NULL,
  week_min_days = NULL,
  hemisphere = NULL,
  partial = NULL,
  invalid = NULL,
  future = NULL,
  as_of = NULL
)

omop_date(reference, date_spec = NULL, broadcast = FALSE)

omop_date_components(
  year,
  month = NULL,
  day = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  which = "first",
  n = 1L,
  scope = "person",
  search = NULL
)

omop_date_parts(
  reference,
  parts = c("year", "month", "day"),
  date_spec = NULL,
  broadcast = FALSE
)

omop_time_between(
  from,
  to,
  unit = "days",
  absolute = FALSE,
  rounding = "none",
  date_spec = NULL,
  broadcast = FALSE
)

omop_age_at(
  reference = "index",
  unit = "years",
  bands = FALSE,
  age_breaks = NULL,
  date_spec = NULL,
  broadcast = FALSE
)

Arguments

precision

Calendar period, day, relative_days or custom.

representation

auto, factor, number, start or end.

numeric

index or decimal_year period coordinate.

origin

Fixed ISO origin for numeric period indices (default 1970-01-01).

anchor

Relative-days anchor.

pattern

Closed calendar pattern; ISO weeks require %G-W%V.

labels

Named public calendar label map; labels must remain unique.

level_range

Two inclusive public ISO dates declaring factor periods.

fiscal_start

Fiscal starting month (1..12).

week_start, week_min_days

Explicit epidemiological week profile (1..7).

hemisphere

north or south, for meteorological seasons.

partial

none, start, mid or end, for incomplete dates.

invalid

na (invalid row values remain missing).

future

allow or na; na requires a fixed as_of.

as_of

Fixed ISO future-policy cutoff.

reference, from, to

Date sources: anchor, ISO date, index, index_end, observation_start/end, birth, death, first_visit or last_visit.

date_spec

Optional omop_date_spec declaration.

broadcast

Repeat a roster value in long event rows.

year, month, day

Integer literals or registered integer source columns.

event

Optional event source for components (default person).

which, n, scope, search

Existing anchor row-selection semantics.

parts

Unique date parts; named entries supply exact final column names.

unit

days, weeks, months, years or decimal_years; age also annual_years.

absolute

Absolute elapsed time (default signed to minus from).

rounding

none, floor, ceiling, trunc or nearest (ties to even).

bands

Return ordered age bands (years/annual_years only).

age_breaks

Integer lower bounds beginning at zero; default 0,5,...,100.

Value

A date specification, source, variable or variable bundle.

Details

Calendar precisions are day, year, semester, quarter, month, iso_week, cdc_week, epi_week, fiscal_year, fiscal_semester, fiscal_quarter, fiscal_month, relative_days and custom. ISO weeks start Monday with four new-year days in week 1; CDC weeks start Sunday with four. epi_week requires both week_start and week_min_days. Fiscal year labels name the starting year. Numeric periods count from the period containing origin (zero); year and fiscal_year instead return the year. decimal_year is a period coordinate, not an elapsed-year fraction. start/end return inclusive period bounds.

Parts are year, semester, quarter, month, month_name, month_abbr, day, weekday, weekday_name, weekday_abbr, iso_week, iso_year, day_of_year, epi_week, epi_year, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, season, month_sin, month_cos, weekday_sin, weekday_cos, season_sin and season_cos. Month/weekday/season categories have full ordered public domains. Names use fixed English. Monday is weekday 1. Northern seasons are Winter, Spring, Summer, Autumn (December-February first); southern names are Summer, Autumn, Winter, Spring. Cyclic values use 2*pi*(k-1)/P with P=12, 7 or 4. Ordered factors use ordered-factor contrasts; request number for a trend coordinate. Shared unused periods are zero-count levels.

Custom patterns accept only %Y, %m, %d, %j, %G, %V, %u, %b, %B, %a, %A, %% and ASCII letters, digits, space or -_/.,:(). ISO %G and %V must appear together without %Y. No locale, code or time-of-day directives are evaluated. Public labels must be unique and cannot merge date categories. level_range declares additional levels and never filters observed dates.

Gregorian dates cover 0001-01-01 through 9999-12-31. Partial dates with partial=none retain only invariant coarsened periods/parts; exact age is NA. start/mid/end impute the first/middle/last possible day and produce estimated ages. Invalid components cannot be repaired. annual_years explicitly returns calendar-year age, including partial births. Negative age is NA. Elapsed months clamp the original day; elapsed years use completed anniversaries; decimal years divide the remainder by the next anniversary interval. A fixed as_of is required for future=na. Bind a fixed date instead of today to make the plan reproducible. Missing anchors retain all roster rows.

An explicit empty spec selects native Date presentation for first_date and last_date reducers; an omitted spec preserves legacy offsets. Native helpers need language 2 at every selected site. Explicit overlapping date_handling refuses; use date_spec for that policy. No owner date permission is required on assignment. Existing publication, metadata support and aggregate gates still apply. Only symbols and disclosure-checked aggregates reach analysts.

Examples

omop_age_at("death")
omop_date("first_visit", omop_date_spec(precision = "quarter"))
omop_date_parts("first_visit", c(visit_year = "year", visit_month = "month"))
